idiom_name: `readonly` class with a private constructor, static factory and hand-written `equals`
implementation_notes: TypeScript's `readonly` is erased at runtime and structural typing is a compile-time relation only, so `===`, `Set` and `Map` still compare references and a value object needs a hand-written `equals` plus a stable hash/serialised key helper. Use `readonly` properties (or `as const`) for compile-time intent, a private constructor with a validating static factory for invariants, and `Object.freeze` when runtime immutability matters; Immutable.js or branded types are the alternatives when the manual equality rule cannot be enforced project-wide.
pitfalls: `readonly` stops nothing at runtime and does not affect assignability: a `readonly` value is compatible with a mutable one, so without `Object.freeze` and a private constructor the value can still be changed.
Structural typing accepts a plain object literal wherever `Money` is expected, so `equals` can receive a value that never passed through the factory - validate at the boundary.
Without a hash/serialised-key helper, `Set`/`Map` cannot deduplicate values, and `Object.is`-based memoization (React dependency arrays, TanStack Query) treats equal values as different.
